alicia: Quick async Q — I'm opening a tiny Terraform change to create a dedicated GPU nodepool for low-latency inference (separate from our batch training pool). TL;DR: want capacity reservations for on-demand baseline + spot fallback. Can folks eyeball the plan and call out obvious gotchas?

ben_m: +1. Can you paste the TF snippet you're planning? main concern is autoscaler interplay + labels/taints so inference pods don't land on spot-only nodes when we need strict SLOs.

alicia: sure — plan is roughly: one ASG with mixed instances, a small on-demand weighted capacity (capacity_reservation for baseline), and a spot fallback ASG if the reservation can't cover. Something like:
```hcl
resource "aws_launch_template" "gpu_lt" {
  name_prefix = "gpu-node-"
  # user_data sets kubelet opts, etc.
}

resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "gpu_inference_asg" {
  mixed_instances_policy {
    launch_template { launch_template_specification { launch_template_id = aws_launch_template.gpu_lt.id } }
    instances_distribution { on_demand_base_capacity = 2 }
  }
  min_size = 2
  max_size = 10
  tags = [{ key = "k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled", value = "true", propagate_at_launch = true }]
}
```

carla_ops: A couple of thoughts:
- Make sure the LT sets node labels (e.g., node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true) and the kubelet has the right --node-labels. Otherwise scheduling will be messy.
- Taint inference nodes with `dedicated=inference:NoSchedule` and use tolerations on the inference DaemonSet/Deployment.

dmitri_r: Why not a single ASG with mixed instances and on_demand_base_capacity? Two ASGs (one reserved, one spot) adds complexity. With mixed policy you can set `on_demand_base_capacity = 2` and `on_demand_percentage_above_base = 50` to guarantee baseline on-demand. AWS will still launch spot for the rest. Also consider `capacity_reservation_specification` if you want location-level reservations (but that gets more ops).

alicia: Good point. I debated the separate ASGs approach because we want absolute isolation of reserved capacity for inference (so training never steals it). If cluster-autoscaler ever scales down the mixed pool, we might lose reserved capacity guarantees. Does a capacity reservation really bind to ASG instances or to AZ/instance?

dmitri_r: Capacity reservations are per AZ/instance type when you create them. If you want a strict guarantee, you can create Capacity Reservations and then use a launch template that targets those AZs/instance-types. But managing lifecycle is annoying. For many teams the mixed_instances_policy + proper autoscaler priority and PodPriority is enough.

esther: Also: secrets/hook for the NVIDIA driver/installers — how are we distributing that? We pulled drivers via an image in the past, but for air-gapped/private customers we keep driver bundles in S3 with KMS encryption and a pod init step that pulls them using IRSA. If you use IRSA, ensure the node IAM role doesn't have broad S3 access — prefer a role-per-nodepool pattern or a short-lived signed URL generator from the control plane.

alicia: For public-hosted clusters we'll use the driver image (ECR) to keep things simple. For Private deployments we need the S3/KMS flow. I need to wire the Terraform to create an IRSA role that the nodepool attaches. Sample snippet: 
```hcl
module "irsa" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-internal/irsa-module"
  name   = "gpu-nodepool-irsa"
  policies = [aws_iam_policy.gpu_s3_access.arn]
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "attach" {
  role       = module.irsa.role_name
  policy_arn = aws_iam_policy.gpu_s3_access.arn
}
```

carla_ops: Make sure the TF plan also sets the kubelet extra args for `--provider-id` and `--cloud-provider` where needed, otherwise the CC/CS: node registration can be flaky. Also we need `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type` label so our nodeSelector + HA scheduling works.

ben_m: About kube-scheduler/priority — if inference pods have higher PodPriority, cluster-autoscaler might evict lower-priority pods to free up nodes, but it won't magically move training pods off reserved nodes. Use `nodeAffinity` + `RequiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` to keep training off inference nodes.

deploy-bot: infra-plan check: 1 error, 2 warnings. Error: subnet mapping missing for AZ b. (run `terraform plan -target=aws_subnet.xyz` to inspect)

alicia: thanks deploy-bot — I'll fix the subnet mapping.

dmitri_r: Also consider taint-based eviction for preemptible/spot nodes: add a taint `spot=true:PreferNoSchedule` and make spot-backed instances carry that taint. Then inference pods won't land unless they have the toleration. That way if spot capacity vanishes, we don't suddenly lose critical inference pods.

esther: For canary rollout, add a small scale-up policy pinned to a specific ASG so we can test new drivers or kernel modules safely. And ensure your nodepool Terraform exposes a tag that we can query from Console -> metrics (eg: team=infra, pool=inference).

alicia: action items I got: 1) switch to single ASG with mixed_instances_policy + on_demand_base_capacity, 2) add node labels & taints in launch template, 3) add IRSA role wiring for private driver pulls, 4) fix subnet AZ mapping from deploy-bot. I'll send a PR that updates the plan and include the kubelet user-data snippet.

carla_ops: LGTM, ping me on the PR for a quick manifest review.

ben_m: I'll review infra PR for autoscaler interactions. Also add a `k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/node-template/label` tag so CA understands pool capacity.

alicia: thanks all. will post PR link once ready :thumbsup:
